While he was injury-prone in his early career, he was able to decrease his injury count by running less off the ball, and by adopting a stricter diet, training regime, and sleep schedule.[[280]](#cite_note-302)

### Tactical positioning

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/0e/Argentina_team_in_St._Petersburg_%28cropped%29_Messi.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Argentina_team_in_St._Petersburg_(cropped)_Messi.jpg)

A versatile forward, Messi often plays as a classic [number 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midfielder#Attacking_midfielder "Midfielder").

Tactically, Messi plays in a free attacking role; a versatile player, he is capable of attacking on either wing or through the centre of the pitch. His favoured position in childhood was the playmaker behind two strikers, known as the *enganche* in Argentine football, but he began his career in Spain as a [left-winger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football_positions#Winger "Association football positions") or [left-sided forward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_(association_football)#Second_striker "Forward (association football)").[[281]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBalagué2013155–156,_405–406-303) Upon his first-team debut, he was moved onto the right wing by manager [Frank Rijkaard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Rijkaard "Frank Rijkaard"); from this position, he could more easily cut through the defence into the middle of the pitch and [curl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curl_(football) "Curl (football)") shots on goal with his left foot, rather than predominantly [cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_(football) "Cross (football)") balls for teammates.[[263]](#cite_note-FTMag-281) Under Guardiola and subsequent managers, he most often played in a [false nine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_(association_football)#False_9 "Forward (association football)") role; positioned as a [centre-forward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_(association_football)#Centre-forward "Forward (association football)") or lone [striker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_(association_football)#Striker "Forward (association football)"), he roamed the centre, often moving deep into midfield and drawing defenders with him, in order to create and exploit spaces for passes, other teammates' attacking runs off the ball, his own dribbling runs, or combinations with Xavi and Iniesta.[[47]](#cite_note-BoyGenius-53)

Under the stewardship of Barcelona manager [Luis Enrique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique "Luis Enrique"), Messi returned to playing in the right-sided position that characterised much of his early career. He played in the manager's 4–3–3 formation,[[282]](#cite_note-304)[[283]](#cite_note-305) and was increasingly deployed in a deeper, free playmaking role in later seasons.[[284]](#cite_note-306)[[285]](#cite_note-improvement-307) Under [Ernesto Valverde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernesto_Valverde "Ernesto Valverde"), Messi played in a variety of roles. While he was still occasionally deployed in a deeper role—from which he could make runs into the box, on the right wing or as a false nine—he was also used in a more offensive, central role in a 4–2–3–1.[[286]](#cite_note-308)[[285]](#cite_note-improvement-307) He was also used as a second striker in a 4–4–2 formation, where he was once again given the licence to drop deep, link up with midfielders, orchestrate his team's attacking plays, and create chances for his attacking partner [Luis Suárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Suárez_(Uruguayan_footballer) "Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)").[[287]](#cite_note-309)[[288]](#cite_note-310) With the Argentina national team, Messi has similarly played anywhere along the frontline. Under various managers, he has been employed on the right wing, as a false nine, as an out-and-out striker, in a supporting role alongside another forward, or in a deeper, free creative role as a classic number 10 playmaker or [attacking midfielder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midfielder#Attacking_midfielder "Midfielder") behind the strikers.[[224]](#cite_note-NewRole-239)[[289]](#cite_note-311)

### Reception

Messi is widely regarded as one of the two best players of his generation, alongside Portuguese forward [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo "Cristiano Ronaldo").[[290]](#cite_note-RonaldoRivalry-312) He is also considered one of the greatest footballers in the history of the sport.[[291]](#cite_note-goat-313) In 2025, he was named the [All Time Men's World Best Player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IFFHS#Top_10_players_of_all-time_(2025) "IFFHS") by the [IFFHS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IFFHS "IFFHS").[[292]](#cite_note-314)

A prodigious talent as a teenager, Messi established himself among the world's best players before age 20.[[293]](#cite_note-315) After winning the [2005 Ballon d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Ballon_d'Or "2005 Ballon d'Or"), Messi's teammate [Ronaldinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronaldinho "Ronaldinho") remarked, "I'm not even the best at Barça" in reference to the 18-year-old Messi.[[294]](#cite_note-316) Four years later, after Messi won his first [Ballon d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballon_d'Or "Ballon d'Or") by a record margin,[[89]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBalagué2013519–524-98) the public debate regarding his qualities as a player moved beyond his status in contemporary football to the possibility that he was one of the greatest players in history.[[W]](#cite_note-318) An early proponent was his then-[Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") manager [Pep Guardiola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pep_Guardiola "Pep Guardiola"), who, as early as August 2009, described Messi as the best player he had ever seen and would ever see.[[296]](#cite_note-319) In the following years, this opinion gained greater acceptance among pundits, managers, former and current players.[[97]](#cite_note-Sublime-107)[[297]](#cite_note-320) By the end of Barcelona's second treble-winning season, the perception of Messi as one of the greatest footballers of all time had become the apparent view among many fans and pundits in continental Europe.[[298]](#cite_note-Telegraph_2016-321)[[299]](#cite_note-322)

Many of Messi's teammates at Barcelona and Argentina have publicly marveled over his talent, including [Thierry Henry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thierry_Henry "Thierry Henry"), [Zlatan Ibrahimović](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zlatan_Ibrahimović "Zlatan Ibrahimović"), [Neymar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neymar "Neymar"), [Luis Suárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Suárez_(Uruguayan_footballer) "Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)"), [Xavi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavi_(footballer,_born_1980) "Xavi (footballer, born 1980)"), [Ángel Di María](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ángel_Di_María "Ángel Di María") and [Javier Mascherano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javier_Mascherano "Javier Mascherano").[[X]](#cite_note-330) Superstar peers [Thomas Müller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Müller "Thomas Müller"), [Eden Hazard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eden_Hazard "Eden Hazard"), [Wayne Rooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Rooney "Wayne Rooney"), [David Beckham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Beckham "David Beckham") and [Didier Drogba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Didier_Drogba "Didier Drogba") have lauded Messi as the greatest player of all time, or the best of his generation.[[Y]](#cite_note-336) Longtime [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid "Real Madrid") rivals [Luka Modrić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Modrić "Luka Modrić") and [Sergio Ramos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Ramos "Sergio Ramos") have both proclaimed Messi the best player in history.[[312]](#cite_note-337)[[313]](#cite_note-338) Messi was a childhood idol for [Jamal Musiala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamal_Musiala "Jamal Musiala"), [Lamine Yamal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamine_Yamal "Lamine Yamal"), [Cole Palmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cole_Palmer "Cole Palmer"), [Estêvão Willian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estêvão_Willian "Estêvão Willian"), [Julián Alvarez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julián_Alvarez "Julián Alvarez") and [Enzo Fernández](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enzo_Fernández "Enzo Fernández").[[Z]](#cite_note-345)

Messi received dismissals by critics throughout his career because he had not won an international tournament at the senior level with Argentina.[[AA]](#cite_note-349) However, his subsequent victories in the [2021 Copa América](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_América "2021 Copa América") and the [2022 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup") resulted in him finally winning every top tier trophy at both the club and country levels, an achievement that many pundits felt cemented Messi's legacy.[[291]](#cite_note-goat-313)

### Rivalry with Cristiano Ronaldo

Main article: [Messi–Ronaldo rivalry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Messi–Ronaldo_rivalry "Messi–Ronaldo rivalry")

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d6/Cristiano_Ronaldo_and_Lionel_Messi_-_Portugal_vs_Argentina%2C_9th_February_2011.jpg/250px-Cristiano_Ronaldo_and_Lionel_Messi_-_Portugal_vs_Argentina%2C_9th_February_2011.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cristiano_Ronaldo_and_Lionel_Messi_-_Portugal_vs_Argentina,_9th_February_2011.jpg)

Messi has been compared with [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo "Cristiano Ronaldo") (left) throughout much of their careers.

Among his contemporary peers, Messi is most often compared and contrasted with [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo "Cristiano Ronaldo"), who many consider his [career rival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Messi–Ronaldo_rivalry "Messi–Ronaldo rivalry").[[290]](#cite_note-RonaldoRivalry-312) Both achieved numerous individual accolades, won dozens of trophies for both club and country, and are the two [leading goal scorers in history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_footballers_with_500_or_more_goals "List of footballers with 500 or more goals"). Although Messi has at times denied any rivalry,[[323]](#cite_note-350)[[324]](#cite_note-351) they are widely believed to push one another in their aim to be the best player in the world.[[325]](#cite_note-Overtaken-352) Pundits have compared the ongoing rivalry to [past sports rivalries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_sports_rivalries "List of sports rivalries") like the [Muhammad Ali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad_Ali "Muhammad Ali")–[Joe Frazier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Frazier "Joe Frazier") rivalry in boxing, the [Prost–Senna rivalry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prost–Senna_rivalry "Prost–Senna rivalry") in motorsport, and the tennis rivalries between [Federer–Nadal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federer–Nadal_rivalry "Federer–Nadal rivalry") and [Borg–McEnroe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borg–McEnroe_rivalry "Borg–McEnroe rivalry").[[326]](#cite_note-353)

Fans and pundits alike regularly argue the individual merits of both players.[[325]](#cite_note-Overtaken-352)[[327]](#cite_note-354) Messi is lauded for his combination of dribbling, playmaking, passing and goalscoring, while Ronaldo has received praise for his exceptional speed and athleticism, goalscoring skills, and performance under pressure.[[328]](#cite_note-355)[[329]](#cite_note-356) Beyond their playing styles, the debate also revolves around their differing physiques – Ronaldo is 1.87 m (6 ft 1+1⁄2 in) with a muscular build, while Messi is much shorter at 1.70 m (5 ft 7 in) – and their contrasting public personalities, with Ronaldo's self-confidence and theatrics differing from Messi's humility.[[330]](#cite_note-357) Regarding individual achievements, Messi has won eight Ballons d'Or to Ronaldo's five,[[331]](#cite_note-358) eight [FIFA World's Best Player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Best_FIFA_Men's_Player#FIFA_Player_of_the_Year_(including_predecessors) "The Best FIFA Men's Player") awards to Ronaldo's five, and six [European Golden Shoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Golden_Shoe "European Golden Shoe") to Ronaldo's four.[[332]](#cite_note-359) Off the pitch, Ronaldo is his direct competitor in terms of salary, sponsorships, and social media fanbase.[[333]](#cite_note-50million-360)

Messi's [head-to-head record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Messi-Ronaldo_rivalry#Head-to-head_summary "Messi-Ronaldo rivalry") against teams that feature Ronaldo consists of 15 wins, 9 draws, and 10 losses in competitive club matches. The first competitive matchup between the two occurred in 2008, when Ronaldo's [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United "Manchester United") played Messi's Barcelona in the [2007–08 UEFA Champions League semi-finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007–08_UEFA_Champions_League_knockout_stage#Semi-finals "2007–08 UEFA Champions League knockout stage"); [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United "Manchester United") advanced and eventually won the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2008 UEFA Champions League final").[[334]](#cite_note-361) The two players and their club teams met again in the next year's [Champions League final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2009 UEFA Champions League final"), with Messi and Barcelona achieving a 2–0 victory.[[335]](#cite_note-362) After this, Ronaldo transferred to [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid "Real Madrid"), the main rivals of Barcelona, which resulted in Messi facing Ronaldo many times in *[El Clásico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Clásico "El Clásico")*, which ranks among the world's most viewed annual sports events.[[336]](#cite_note-363)[[333]](#cite_note-50million-360) A number of football critics, commentators, and players have said that Messi's triumph with Argentina in the 2022 World Cup has settled the contest between the two players.[[AB]](#cite_note-367)

### Comparisons with Diego Maradona

Main article: [New Maradona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Maradona "New Maradona")

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/Maradona_vs_england.jpg/250px-Maradona_vs_england.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Maradona_vs_england.jpg)

Due to their similar stature and style of play, Messi has frequently been compared to his compatriot [Diego Maradona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Maradona "Diego Maradona").

Throughout his career, Messi has been compared with [Diego Maradona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Maradona "Diego Maradona"), who was also considered the best player of his generation and one of the greatest in the history of the sport.[[340]](#cite_note-adept-368)[[341]](#cite_note-369) The comparisons stem broadly from both players' short statures, their similar playing styles as left-footed [playmakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Playmaker "Playmaker"), and their shared nationality as Argentines.[[342]](#cite_note-Daily-370) Initially, Messi was merely one of many young Argentine players to receive the "[New Maradona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Maradona "New Maradona")" moniker, but as his career progressed, he proved his similarity beyond all previous contenders, establishing himself as the best player Argentina had produced since Maradona.[[44]](#cite_note-Aimar-50)[[343]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELisi2011533–539-371) When Messi was 18 years old, Maradona called him the best player in the world and hailed him as his successor.[[344]](#cite_note-successor-372) From 2008 through the [2010 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_FIFA_World_Cup "2010 FIFA World Cup"), Messi played for Argentina's [national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina_national_football_team "Argentina national football team") with Maradona as his manager, and it was during this period that Messi was given the number 10 shirt that Maradona famously wore. Maradona gave Messi his blessing, telling him: "the No 10 is yours. There's nobody better than you to wear it."[[223]](#cite_note-telegraph.co.uk-238)

During the early and middle parts of Messi's career, he was generally held in lesser esteem than Maradona in Argentine society. Part of this had to do with Messi's lack of international tournament success and perceived uneven output with the national team; Maradona had famously led Argentina to victory in the [1986 FIFA World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_FIFA_World_Cup "1986 FIFA World Cup"), which set an expectation for Messi to do the same.[[AC]](#cite_note-373) Argentines also identified more with the fiery, extroverted and controversial Maradona who came from the slums, as opposed to the reserved, introverted and unassuming Messi who had a comparably unremarkable upbringing in Rosario.[[AD]](#cite_note-375) Maradona, along with several pundits and footballing figures, questioned whether Messi's temperament made him a capable leader for the national team.[[AE]](#cite_note-378) Furthermore, Messi's lack of outward passion for the Argentina shirt, his early tendency not to sing the national anthem, and his relative lack of emotional displays have led to a perception that he feels more Catalan than Argentine.[[225]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBalagué2013414–420-240)[[348]](#cite_note-Vickery-379) However, despite having lived in Barcelona since age 13, Messi rejected the option of representing Spain internationally, saying: "Argentina is my country, my family, my way of expressing myself. I would change all my records to make the people in my country happy."[[349]](#cite_note-380)

> "I have seen the player who will inherit my place in Argentinian football and his name is Messi."

— [Diego Maradona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Maradona "Diego Maradona") hailing the 18-year-old Messi as his successor in February 2006[[344]](#cite_note-successor-372)

Football journalist [Tim Vickery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Vickery "Tim Vickery") said the perception of Messi among Argentines changed in 2019, when Messi made a conscious effort to become "more one of the group, more Argentine".[[348]](#cite_note-Vickery-379) Other pundits noted that Messi had grown more assertive as a leader during the [2019 Copa América](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Copa_América "2019 Copa América") by becoming more vocal with his teammates both on and off the pitch, finally singing the national anthem with the team before matches, and speaking with journalists at length after matches.[[350]](#cite_note-381) Following Argentina's 2022 World Cup win, Vickery felt that Messi would now be held in the same esteem by his compatriots as Maradona.[[348]](#cite_note-Vickery-379) Journalist and former footballer [Jorge Valdano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Valdano "Jorge Valdano") said he saw a "Maradonian" edge to Messi's performances during the tournament, while his compatriot [Osvaldo Ardiles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osvaldo_Ardiles "Osvaldo Ardiles") said that Messi's provocative actions towards the Netherlands team during the [quarter-final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Lusail "Battle of Lusail") resembled Maradona's behavior, which further endeared Messi to his fellow Argentines.[[351]](#cite_note-382)[[352]](#cite_note-ArdilesMessi-383) Messi himself later remarked that the World Cup victory "won over all the people of Argentina. Today 95% or 100% of Argentines love me and that's a beautiful feeling."[[353]](#cite_note-384)

## Cultural impact and legacy

### Popularity

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cd/Lionel_MESSI_Florent_TORCHUT.jpg/250px-Lionel_MESSI_Florent_TORCHUT.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Lionel_MESSI_Florent_TORCHUT.jpg)

Messi (right) being interviewed in 2019 by [France Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_Football "France Football"). Messi's success on the pitch has earned him widespread recognition and popularity.

Messi was among the [*Time* 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_100 "Time 100"), an annual list of the world's most influential people, in 2011, 2012 and 2023.[[AF]](#cite_note-388) According to a 2014 survey in 15 international markets, Messi was familiar to 87% of respondents around the world, of whom 78% perceived him favourably, making him the second-most recognised player globally, behind [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo "Cristiano Ronaldo"), and the most likeable of all contemporary players.[[357]](#cite_note-389)[[358]](#cite_note-390) [World Press Photo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Press_Photo "World Press Photo") selected "The Final Game", a photo of Messi facing the [World Cup trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_Trophy "FIFA World Cup Trophy") after Argentina's final defeat to Germany, as the best sports image of 2014.[[359]](#cite_note-391)

Messi's fanbase on [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook") is among the largest of public figures: by July 2023, he had [more than 114 million followers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-followed_Facebook_pages "List of most-followed Facebook pages"), the second highest for an athlete after Cristiano Ronaldo.[[360]](#cite_note-392)[[361]](#cite_note-393) Messi has over 500 million [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") followers, the [second highest for an individual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-followed_Instagram_accounts "List of most-followed Instagram accounts") and athlete after Ronaldo.[[362]](#cite_note-394) Messi's World Cup celebration post from 18 December 2022 is the [most liked post on Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-liked_Instagram_posts "List of most-liked Instagram posts") with more than 75 million likes.[[363]](#cite_note-395) In April 2023, Messi was featured in the [Thrissur Pooram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrissur_Pooram "Thrissur Pooram") festival in [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"), India.[[364]](#cite_note-396)[[365]](#cite_note-397) In December 2023, a set of shirts Messi had worn during the 2022 World Cup was sold at auction for $7.8 million.[[366]](#cite_note-398)

During an [exhibition match on 4 February 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong_v_Inter_Miami "Hong Kong v Inter Miami") between Inter Miami and [Hong Kong League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong_League "Hong Kong League") players at [Hong Kong Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hong_Kong_Stadium "Hong Kong Stadium"), Messi remained on the bench the entire game. His absence from the pitch caused massive backlash in Hong Kong and China, as thousands of spectators had hoped to see him play.[[367]](#cite_note-399) One Messi commercial was taken off the air in those regions,[[368]](#cite_note-400) while other commercials continued to air despite pressure from Chinese social-media users.[[AG]](#cite_note-404) The [Chinese Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Football_Association "Chinese Football Association") temporarily halted its partnership with the [Argentine Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentine_Football_Association "Argentine Football Association") over the incident.[[372]](#cite_note-405)

### Wealth and sponsorships

In 2026, [Bloomberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloomberg_News "Bloomberg News") reported that Messi's net worth had surpassed $1 billion.[[373]](#cite_note-406) Messi was the world's highest-paid footballer for five out of six years between 2009 and 2014. His salary broke records in 2013 (€41 million) and 2014 (€65 million).[[374]](#cite_note-407)[[375]](#cite_note-408) *[Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")* listed him as the world's second highest-paid athlete in 2016, and as the [world's highest-paid athlete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes'_list_of_the_world's_highest-paid_athletes "Forbes' list of the world's highest-paid athletes") in 2019.[[AH]](#cite_note-412) In 2018, he was the first player to exceed the €100 million benchmark for a calendar year, with earnings of €126 million in combined income from salaries, bonuses and endorsements.[[379]](#cite_note-413)[[380]](#cite_note-414) In 2020, Messi became the second footballer to surpass $1 billion in career earnings.[[381]](#cite_note-415) In 2026, he appeared on *[The World's Billionaires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_World's_Billionaires "The World's Billionaires")* list for the first time with a $1.1 billion net worth.[[382]](#cite_note-416)

In addition to salary and bonuses, much of Messi's income comes from endorsements. His brand was at first based exclusively on his talents and achievements as a player, in contrast to arguably more glamorous players like Ronaldo and [David Beckham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Beckham "David Beckham"). At the start of his career, Messi mainly held sponsorship contracts with companies that employed sports-oriented marketing, such as [Adidas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adidas "Adidas") and Pepsi.[[383]](#cite_note-417)[[384]](#cite_note-Fourth-418) Since 2006, Adidas has been his largest sponsor, and he eventually became the company's leading brand endorser.[[385]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTECaioli201294–97-419)[[333]](#cite_note-50million-360) Starting in 2010, Messi's marketing appeal broadened as he reached higher achievements as a player. He signed long-term endorsement deals with luxury brands [Dolce & Gabbana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolce_&_Gabbana "Dolce & Gabbana") and [Audemars Piguet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audemars_Piguet "Audemars Piguet"),[[384]](#cite_note-Fourth-418)[[386]](#cite_note-420) and became a [brand ambassador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brand_ambassador "Brand ambassador") for [Gillette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gillette_(brand) "Gillette (brand)"), [Turkish Airlines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_Airlines "Turkish Airlines"), [Ooredoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ooredoo "Ooredoo"), and [Tata Motors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tata_Motors "Tata Motors"), among other companies.[[AI]](#cite_note-425) Messi has also been the face of two video game series: [Konami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konami "Konami")'s *[Pro Evolution Soccer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Evolution_Soccer "Pro Evolution Soccer")* and [EA Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EA_Sports "EA Sports")' *[FIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_(video_game_series) "FIFA (video game series)")*.[[391]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGuinness_World_Records2014102-426)[[392]](#cite_note-427)

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f6/Hinchas_de_Messi.jpg/250px-Hinchas_de_Messi.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hinchas_de_Messi.jpg)

Messi's Argentina jersey, supplied by Adidas, was sold out worldwide during the 2022 World Cup.[[393]](#cite_note-Arg_sales-428)

*[SportsPro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SportsPro "SportsPro")* cited Messi as one of the world's most marketable athletes every year between 2010 and 2015.[[394]](#cite_note-429) He became the first footballer to receive his own sub-brand of Adidas boots, the Adidas Messi, in 2015.[[395]](#cite_note-430)[[396]](#cite_note-431) The same year, a Barcelona jersey with Messi's name and number was the best-selling replica jersey worldwide.[[397]](#cite_note-432) During the 2022 World Cup, Adidas sold out of Messi's No. 10 Argentina jersey worldwide.[[393]](#cite_note-Arg_sales-428)

In 2013, a Turkish Airlines advertisement starring Messi and [Kobe Bryant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kobe_Bryant "Kobe Bryant") became the most-watched advertisement on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"), with 137 million views. It was voted by users as the best advertisement of the decade 2005–2015.[[398]](#cite_note-433)[[399]](#cite_note-434) In June 2021, Messi signed a five-year deal to become a brand ambassador for [Hard Rock Cafe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_Rock_Cafe "Hard Rock Cafe"),[[400]](#cite_note-435) and the following year he became a tourism ambassador for [Saudi Arabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia "Saudi Arabia"). He was criticised for partnering with Saudi Arabia because of the country's poor record on human rights.[[401]](#cite_note-436)[[402]](#cite_note-437)

The statue of Messi stands alongside statues of [Pelé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelé "Pelé") and Maradona.[[409]](#cite_note-444) In December 2025, during Messi's [tour of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi's_2025_India_Tour "Lionel Messi's 2025 India Tour"), a 70-foot (21 m) statue of him holding the World Cup trophy was unveiled at the Sree Bhumi Sporting Club in [Lake Town, Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Town,_Kolkata "Lake Town, Kolkata").[[410]](#cite_note-445) The statue was later removed due to instability. In June 2026, an 85-foot (26 m) [statue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cutral_Co_Messi_Statue "Cutral Co Messi Statue") of Messi was erected in [Cutral Có](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cutral_Có "Cutral Có"), Argentina.[[411]](#cite_note-446)

### Business ventures

On 4 June 2024, Messi announced the release of [Más+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Más+ "Más+"), an American brand of [sports drinks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_drink "Sports drink") and [energy drinks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energy_drink "Energy drink").[[414]](#cite_note-SafidDeen2024-449) Messi created the drinks because he could not find a flavourful and healthy hydration option that suited his needs.[[AJ]](#cite_note-452) On 19 September, Messi launched the production company 525 Rosario, which produces films, sporting events coverage and branded commercials for athletes worldwide. It is a joint venture with Smuggler Entertainment, which co-produced *Messi's World Cup: The Rise of a Legend* earlier in 2024.[[417]](#cite_note-453) In 2025, Messi was invited by his [Inter Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_Miami_CF "Inter Miami CF") teammate [Luis Suárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Suárez_(Uruguayan_footballer) "Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)") to play a role in [Deportivo LSM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deportivo_LSM "Deportivo LSM"), the Uruguayan professional football club that Suárez founded.[[418]](#cite_note-454) On 16 April 2026, Messi acquired full ownership of the Spanish football club [UE Cornellà](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UE_Cornellà "UE Cornellà").[[419]](#cite_note-455)

## Philanthropy

Throughout his career, Messi has been involved in charitable efforts aimed at children, a commitment that stems in part from the medical difficulties he faced in his own childhood. Since 2004, he has contributed his time and finances to the [United Nations Children's Fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNICEF "UNICEF") (UNICEF), an organisation that has also collaborated with [FC Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona").[[420]](#cite_note-Leo_Messi:_Goodwill_Ambassador-456)[[421]](#cite_note-457) Messi has served as a [UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNICEF_Goodwill_Ambassador "UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador") since 2010; he completed his first field mission for the organisation that year as he travelled to Haiti to bring awareness to the plight of the country's children following the [2010 Haiti earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_Haiti_earthquake "2010 Haiti earthquake"). He has since participated in UNICEF campaigns related to [HIV prevention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prevention_of_HIV/AIDS "Prevention of HIV/AIDS"), education, and the social inclusion of disabled children.[[422]](#cite_note-458) In November 2013, Messi and his one-year-old son Thiago were part of a publicity campaign to raise awareness of mortality rates among disadvantaged children.[[423]](#cite_note-459)

In 2007, Messi launched the Leo Messi Foundation, which supports access to health care, education, and sport for children.[[424]](#cite_note-460) It was established following Messi's visit to a hospital in Boston for terminally ill children, an experience that resonated with him to the point that he decided to reinvest part of his earnings into society.[[425]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBalagué2013576–577-461) Through his foundation, Messi has awarded research grants, financed medical training, and invested in the development of medical centres and projects in Argentina, Spain, and elsewhere in the world.[[425]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBalagué2013576–577-461)[[426]](#cite_note-462) In addition to receiving funds from Messi's own fundraising activities, the foundation receives financial support from various companies which have endorsement agreements with Messi, with Adidas as the main sponsor.[[427]](#cite_note-463)[[428]](#cite_note-464) A gold replica of Messi's left foot, weighing 25 kg (55 lb) and valued at $5.3 million, went on sale in Japan in 2013 to raise funds for victims of the [2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Tōhoku_earthquake_and_tsunami "2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami").[[429]](#cite_note-465)

Messi has invested in youth football in Argentina. He supports Sarmiento, a football club based in the Rosario neighbourhood where he was born, and in 2013 he committed to the refurbishment of the club's facilities and the installation of all-weather pitches. Messi also financially supports the management of several youth players at [Newell's Old Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newell's_Old_Boys "Newell's Old Boys") (his boyhood club) and rival club [Rosario Central](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosario_Central "Rosario Central"), as well as at [River Plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Atlético_River_Plate "Club Atlético River Plate") and [Boca Juniors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boca_Juniors "Boca Juniors") in Buenos Aires.[[425]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBalagué2013576–577-461) In 2012, Messi funded the construction of a new gymnasium and a dormitory inside Newell's [stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estadio_Marcelo_Bielsa "Estadio Marcelo Bielsa") for their youth academy. His youth coach at Newell's, Ernesto Vecchio, is employed by the Leo Messi Foundation as a talent scout for young players.[[37]](#cite_note-Here-42) On 7 June 2016, Messi won a libel case against [*La Razón* newspaper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Razón_(Madrid) "La Razón (Madrid)") and was awarded €65,000 in damages, which he donated to the charity [Médecins Sans Frontières](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Médecins_Sans_Frontières "Médecins Sans Frontières").[[430]](#cite_note-466) During the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), Messi and his FC Barcelona teammates announced they would take a 70% salary cut to offset the club's financial losses, and said they would make further contributions to ensure club employees received full salaries while unable to work.[[431]](#cite_note-467) Messi also donated €1 million to fight the spread of COVID-19.[[432]](#cite_note-468)[[433]](#cite_note-469)

In November 2016, while the [Argentine Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentine_Football_Association "Argentine Football Association") was being run by a FIFA committee due to an economic crisis, three of the national team's security staff told Messi that they had not received their salaries for six months. He paid the salaries of the three employees.[[434]](#cite_note-470)[[435]](#cite_note-471) In February 2021, Messi made a donation to the [Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museu_Nacional_d'Art_de_Catalunya "Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya"): the Adidas shoes he wore when he scored his 644th goal for Barcelona and broke [Pelé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelé "Pelé")'s record for most goals scored for a single club. The museum later auctioned off the shoes for £125,000 to support a charity focused on children with cancer.[[436]](#cite_note-472)

Ahead of the [2021 Copa América](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_América "2021 Copa América"), Messi donated three signed sweatshirts to the Chinese pharmaceutical firm [Sinovac Biotech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinovac_Biotech "Sinovac Biotech") – whose directors spoke of their admiration for Messi – in order to secure 50,000 doses of Sinovac's [COVID-19 vaccine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_vaccine "COVID-19 vaccine"), [CoronaVac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CoronaVac "CoronaVac"), in the hope of vaccinating all South American football players. The plan, which was brokered by Uruguay's president [Luis Lacalle Pou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Lacalle_Pou "Luis Lacalle Pou"), caused some controversy for its focus on football players, given widespread vaccine scarcity on the continent.[[437]](#cite_note-Vac-473) In January 2025, Messi was awarded the [Presidential Medal of Freedom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_Medal_of_Freedom "Presidential Medal of Freedom"), the highest civilian award of the United States, for his contributions to healthcare and education programs for children around the world.[[438]](#cite_note-PMOF-474)[[439]](#cite_note-475)

On 4 August 2026, Messi donated €80,000 to support reconstruction efforts in the [Sierra Oeste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Oeste?action=edit&redlink=1 "Sierra Oeste (page does not exist)") [[es](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra%20Oeste%20de%20Madrid "es:Sierra Oeste de Madrid")] region of the [Community of Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_of_Madrid "Community of Madrid") following the [wildfires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Spain_wildfires "2026 Spain wildfires"). [Isabel Díaz Ayuso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isabel_Díaz_Ayuso "Isabel Díaz Ayuso"), President of the Community of Madrid, publicly thanked him for the donation.[[440]](#cite_note-476)

## Personal life

### Family and relationships

Since 2008, Messi has been in a relationship with [Antonela Roccuzzo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonela_Roccuzzo "Antonela Roccuzzo"), whom he married on 30 June 2017 in their home city of [Rosario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosario,_Santa_Fe "Rosario, Santa Fe").[[441]](#cite_note-477)[[442]](#cite_note-478) Roccuzzo is the cousin of Messi's childhood best friend, [Lucas Scaglia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucas_Scaglia "Lucas Scaglia"), and Messi has known her since he was five years old.[[443]](#cite_note-479) After keeping their relationship private for a year, Messi confirmed their romance in an interview in January 2009.[[444]](#cite_note-480) Messi and Roccuzzo have three sons, born in 2012, 2015, and 2018.[[445]](#cite_note-481) To celebrate Roccuzzo's first pregnancy, Messi placed the ball under his shirt after scoring in Argentina's 4–0 win against Ecuador on 2 June 2012, before confirming the pregnancy in an interview two weeks later.[[446]](#cite_note-482) Messi and his family are [Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic "Catholic").[[447]](#cite_note-483)

Messi has a close relationship with his immediate family members, particularly his mother, Celia, whose face is tattooed on his left shoulder. His professional affairs are largely run as a family business. His father [Jorge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Messi "Jorge Messi") was his agent and manager from 2000 until 2026, when he died at the age of 68.[[448]](#cite_note-484) His oldest brother, Rodrigo, handles his daily schedule and publicity. His mother and other brother, Matías, manage his charitable organisation, the Leo Messi Foundation, and take care of personal and professional matters in Rosario.[[449]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBalagué201331,_143,_570-485) His younger sister, María Sol, had a leadership role at Messi's fashion brand The Messi Store before joining his production company 525 Rosario.[[30]](#cite_note-siblings-35)

Since leaving for Spain at age 13, Messi has maintained close ties to Rosario, and has preserved his [Rosarino accent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rioplatense_Spanish "Rioplatense Spanish"). He has retained ownership of his family's old house, although it has long stood empty, and he maintains a penthouse apartment in an exclusive residential building for his mother, as well as a family compound just outside the city. Messi keeps in frequent contact with a small group of confidants in Rosario, most of whom were fellow members of "The Machine of '87" at [Newell's Old Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newell's_Old_Boys "Newell's Old Boys"). He was on bad terms with the club after his transfer to Barcelona, but by 2012 their public feud had ended, with Newell's embracing their ties with Messi and issuing a club membership card to his newborn son.[[AK]](#cite_note-487) Messi has long planned to end his playing career at Newell's.[[451]](#cite_note-488) Messi has citizenship in Argentina, Italy, and Spain.[[452]](#cite_note-489)

### Tax fraud

Messi came under investigation in 2013 for suspected [tax evasion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_evasion "Tax evasion") in Spain. Offshore companies in [tax havens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_haven "Tax haven") such as [Uruguay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uruguay "Uruguay"), [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland "Switzerland") and [Belize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belize "Belize") were used to evade €4.1 million in taxes related to his sponsorship earnings between 2007 and 2009. Messi, who pleaded ignorance to the scheme, voluntarily paid arrears of €5.1 million in August 2013. On 6 July 2016, Messi and his father were both found guilty of tax fraud and were given [suspended](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suspended_sentence "Suspended sentence") 21-month prison sentences and ordered to pay €1.7 million and €1.4 million in fines, respectively.[[453]](#cite_note-490) In court, Messi told the judge, "I just played football. I signed the contracts because I trusted my dad and the lawyers and we had decided that they would take charge of those things." An unrelated [shell company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shell_company "Shell company") in Panama set up in 2012 was subsequently identified as belonging to the Messis in the [Panama Papers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama_Papers "Panama Papers") data leak.[[454]](#cite_note-491)

The Best FIFA Men's Player is an association football award presented annually by the sport's governing body, FIFA, since 2016, to honour the player deemed to have performed the best over the previous calendar year. The award was formerly known as the FIFA World Player of the Year, which was merged with France Football's Ballon d'Or in 2010 to become the FIFA Ballon d'Or in a six-year partnership.

**The Best FIFA Men's Player** is an [association football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") award presented annually by the sport's governing body, [FIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA "FIFA"), since 2016, to honour the player deemed to have performed the best over the previous calendar year.[[1]](#cite_note-1) The award was formerly known as the [FIFA World Player of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Player_of_the_Year "FIFA World Player of the Year"), which was merged with *[France Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_Football "France Football")*'s [Ballon d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballon_d'Or "Ballon d'Or") in 2010 to become the [FIFA Ballon d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_Ballon_d'Or "FIFA Ballon d'Or") in a six-year partnership.[[2]](#cite_note-2)

## History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Best_FIFA_Men%27s_Player&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

In 2010, the [FIFA World Player of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Player_of_the_Year "FIFA World Player of the Year") award combined with the [Ballon d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballon_d'Or "Ballon d'Or") to create the [FIFA Ballon d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_Ballon_d'Or "FIFA Ballon d'Or") in a six-year partnership.[[3]](#cite_note-3) FIFA presided over the FIFA Ballon d'Or after agreeing to pay £13million for the merge of the two major player awards with *[France Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/France_Football "France Football")*. The six editions of the FIFA Ballon d'Or were dominated by [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi") and [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo "Cristiano Ronaldo"), as part of [their ongoing rivalry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo–Lionel_Messi_rivalry "Cristiano Ronaldo–Lionel Messi rivalry"). In 2016, the Ballon d’Or again lost its "FIFA" tag and would be voted for exclusively by journalists, while the FIFA World Player of the Year award – which ran from 1991 to 2009 – was resurrected, this time as The Best FIFA Men's Player.[[4]](#cite_note-4)

According to reports, FIFA's decision not to renew the deal was made in order to improve the organization's strained relationship with England's [FA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Football_Association "The Football Association"). This was based on the fact the annual ceremony was held in [Zürich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zürich "Zürich") – and new FIFA president [Gianni Infantino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gianni_Infantino "Gianni Infantino") wanted to move the next one to [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London").[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

The trophy was designed by Croatian artist Ana Barbić Katičić.[[5]](#cite_note-5)

### Criteria and voting

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Best_FIFA_Men%27s_Player&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Criteria and voting")]

The selection criteria for the players of the year are sporting performance, as well as general conduct on and off the pitch.

The votes are decided by media representatives, national team coaches, and national team captains. In October 2016, it was announced that the general public would also be allowed to vote. Each group has 25% of the overall vote.[[6]](#cite_note-6)

## How The Best FIFA Men’s Player Award winner was determinedHow The Best FIFA Men’s Player Award winner was determined

   From the 12-player shortlist, each voter made their first, second and third choices for the prize.

   Points were given to nominees depending on where they were placed (five points for first, three for second and one for third).

   Nominated national team captains could not vote for themselves.

   Selections from the four voting groups – coaches, captains, journalists, and fans – each counted for 25 per cent of the total vote, irrespective of the number of voters from each group.

   The Best FIFA Men’s Player Award was presented to the individual with the most points.

# Lionel Messi wins The Best FIFA Men's Player Award

Published 15 Jan 2024

Share

Argentina captain retains prestigious prize ahead of fellow finalists Haaland and Mbappe.

![Image 2: FIFA](https://digitalhub.fifa.com/transform/214e9562-7d8f-4b11-a678-d0a1ee39f77a/tbffa23_mens-player_web_3840x1492?&io=transform:fill,width:768&quality=75)

*   **Award recognises most exceptional performer in the men's game from 19 December 2022 to 20 August 2023**

*   **Messi wins prize ahead of finalists Erling Haaland and Kylian Mbappe**

*   **Argentina captain retains title he won in 2022**

Lionel Messi has been crowned The Best FIFA Men’s Player 2023, retaining the title he won in 2022.

The Argentina superstar has been bestowed with the honour once again following another qualifying period where he dazzled football fans across the globe. Messi was recognised for his achievements at The Best FIFA Football Awards™ ceremony in London, having come out on top in the voting ahead of finalists Erling Haaland and Kylian Mbappe.

Messi topped an incredibly closely-contested poll which was voted for by national team coaches and captains as well as expert journalists and supporters across the globe.

With the 2022 World Cup winner and Norway international Haaland locked together on 48 scoring points, they were separated by the number of first-choice nominations which Messi received in votes from national team captains, [as per the Rules of Allocation (article 12)](https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/7abca94c3eb669f2/original/FIFA-Awards-2023_The-Best-Awards_Rules-of-allocation_EN.pdf). France striker Mbappe finished third with 35 points.

[View the full The Best FIFA Men's Player voting breakdown here.](https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/7509d02470633f73/original/The-Best-FIFA-Football-Awards-2023-Result-Breakdown_The-Best-FIFA-Men-s-Player.pdf)

Messi also won the 2019 Best FIFA Men's Player award and was recognised by FIFA as the leading player in the men's game on five occasions prior to that - 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012 and 2015 - making this his eighth individual award in total.

## **The winner in focus****The winner in focus**

Messi is a player who has won everything, claiming an extensive haul of major domestic, international and individual honours to place himself firmly in the category of an all-time great of the beautiful game.

_La Pulga Atomica_ was named The Best Men's Player in 2022 after leading Argentina to FIFA World Cup™ glory in Qatar, and he added further silverware to his trophy collection in 2023 as PSG once again topped the table in France as Ligue 1 champions.

The 36-year-old's two-year spell in Paris came to an end in July, with the all-time top scorer in the top five European leagues heading across the Atlantic for the latest chapter of his career with Inter Miami.

## **Messi's standout moments****Messi's standout moments**

In helping PSG to another domestic title - a second in succession during his spell in France - Messi recorded more assists than any other player during the campaign and was subsequently named in the Ligue 1 Team of the Season.

## **How The Best FIFA Men’s Player Award winner was determined****How The Best FIFA Men’s Player Award winner was determined**

*   From the 12-player shortlist, each voter made their first, second and third choices for the prize.

*   Points were given to nominees depending on where they were placed (five points for first, three for second and one for third).

*   Nominated national team captains could not vote for themselves.

*   Selections from the four voting groups – coaches, captains, journalists, and fans – each counted for 25 per cent of the total vote, irrespective of the number of voters from each group.

*   The Best FIFA Men’s Player Award was presented to the individual with the most points.

*   If finalists were tied on points, the individual with the most first-choice selections from their own group of voters would be declared the winner.

The voting procedure for The Best FIFA Men’s Player Award was supervised by independent observers. Results will be published in full on FIFA.com following the awards ceremony on 15 January 2024.

# The Best FIFA Football Awards: Full List of Past Winners

![Google Discover](https://assets.minutemediacdn.com/platform/google_discover_icon.svg)
![Vinicius Junior was named Best FIFA Men’s Player in 2024.](https://images2.minutemediacdn.com/image/upload/c_crop,x_160,y_54,w_734,h_412/c_fill,w_720,ar_16:9,f_auto,q_auto,g_auto/images/voltaxMediaLibrary/mmsport/si/01kchg1nd8gp2y2r0f0e.jpg "Vinicius Junior was named Best FIFA Men’s Player in 2024.")

Soccer is a team game, but that doesn’t prevent an almighty scramble for individual awards every single year.

The [Ballon d’Or](https://www.si.com/soccer/ballon-dor) might boast the renown and prestige that all other prizes aspire to achieve, but the relatively recent introduction of the Best FIFA Football Awards offers another route to solo stardom for the world’s elite.

There are an array of accolades on offer at the ceremony, which has been staged by world soccer’s governing body since the inaugural event in January 2017. Prizes are distributed based on performances over the calendar year, with both coaches and players earning acclaim.

Here are the past winners across all the Best FIFA Football Awards categories since its inception.

## The Best FIFA Men’s Player: Past Winners

![Lionel Messi](https://images2.minutemediacdn.com/image/upload/c_crop,x_0,y_132,w_4259,h_2839/c_fill,w_16,ar_16:9,f_auto,q_auto,g_auto/images/voltaxMediaLibrary/mmsport/si/01k9vwd1v4f347aq97g5.jpg "Lionel Messi")

Cristiano Ronaldo scooped the first two Best FIFA Men’s Player awards, collecting the prize for 2016 and 2017, but it’s the ex-[Real Madrid](https://www.si.com/soccer/team/real-madrid) star’s longstanding career rival Lionel Messi who has collected the crown most frequently.

The veteran forward triumphed in 2019 with [Barcelona](https://www.si.com/soccer/team/barcelona) and then won successive awards in 2022 and 2023 following his performances for [Paris Saint-Germain](https://www.si.com/soccer/team/paris-saint-germain), [Inter Miami](https://www.si.com/soccer/team/inter-miami-cf) and, most importantly, Argentina.

Robert Lewandowski is tied with Ronaldo in second with two victories, while modern Real Madrid greats Luka Modrić and Vinicius Junior have also clinched the honor previously.

The Best FIFA Men’s Goalkeeper was not crowned in 2016 as Gianluigi Buffon scooped the inaugural title the following year for his displays with Juventus. Thibaut Courtois stole his crown in 2018, representing both [Chelsea](https://www.si.com/soccer/team/chelsea) and Real Madrid, before Alisson and Manuel Neuer proceeded to earn the prize.

But Premier League sides have dominated the award in recent years, with Édouard Mendy winning in 2021 after his Champions League heroics with Chelsea, while [Manchester City](https://www.si.com/soccer/team/manchester-city)’s Ederson ran out victor in 2023—sandwiched in between victories for Aston Villa stopper Emiliano Martínez.

An array of soccer’s elite tactical minds have got their hands on the Best FIFA Men’s Coach award, but only ex-[Liverpool](https://www.si.com/soccer/team/liverpool) manager Jürgen Klopp has won it on more than one occasion. Champions League success in 2019 and Premier League glory in 2020 ensured two successive triumphs.

Claudio Ranieri rightly won the trophy in 2016 after achieving impossible Premier League glory with Leicester City, while Frenchmen Zinedine Zidane and Didier Deschamps followed in the Italian’s footsteps.

Thomas Tuchel, Lionel Scaloni, Pep Guardiola and Carlo Ancelotti have all won since Klopp’s back-to-back titles.

Carli Lloyd won the inaugural prize and was followed by United States compatriot Megan Rapinoe three years later. In between their victories, Lieke Martens and Marta clinched the crown, while Lucy Bronze triumphed in 2020.

O maior vencedor da Bola de Ouro está de volta ao prêmio. E como favorito. Após a rara ausência entre os indicados na edição de 2022, o craque Lionel Messi deve estar na cerimônia da tradicional premiação da revista *France Football* na **próxima segunda-feira**, em Paris. E, segundo a imprensa europeia, deve ser coroado pela oitava vez.

Messi é o maior vencedor do prêmio dado pela revista *France Football* ao melhor do mundo. O jogador do Inter Miami conquistou o troféu sete vezes e lidera o ranking com folga. Cristiano Ronaldo é o segundo da lista, com cinco títulos.

Em 2022, o camisa 10 argentino não foi indicado pela primeira vez desde 2005. Entre 2008 e 2017, ele e o português se revezaram nas duas primeiras posições, com cinco prêmios para cada. Messi venceria depois também em 2019 e 2021.

> A cerimônia da entrega da Bola de Ouro acontece na próxima segunda, dia 30, com transmissão do sportv e live no **ge**

Messi tem 10 prêmios ao todo: sete Bolas de Ouro, quatro delas unificadas com a Fifa, e outros três de Melhor Jogador do Mundo dados pela entidade máxima do futebol.

Veja o histórico, ano a ano, desde que ele passou a aparecer nas premiações individuais.

- 2006: 21º na Bola de Ouro (France Football) e não indicado na Fifa
- 2007: 3º na Bola de Ouro (France Football) e 2º na Fifa
- 2008: 2º na Bola de Ouro (France Football) e 2º na Fifa
- 2009: Bola de Ouro (France Football) e Melhor do Mundo (Fifa)
- 2010: Bola de Ouro (France Football + Fifa)
- 2011: Bola de Ouro (France Football + Fifa)
- 2012: Bola de Ouro (France Football + Fifa)
- 2013: 2º na Bola de Ouro (France Football) e 2º na Fifa
- 2013: 2º na Bola de Ouro (France Football) e 2º na Fifa
- 2015: Bola de Ouro (France Football + Fifa)
- 2016: 2º na Bola de Ouro (France Football) e 2º no The Best (Fifa)
- 2017: 2º na Bola de Ouro (France Football) e 2º no The Best (Fifa)
- 2018: 5º na Bola de Ouro (France Football) e 5º no The Best (Fifa)
- 2019: Bola de Ouro (France Football) e The Best (Fifa)
- 2020: Não houve Bola de Ouro (France Football) | 2º no The Best (Fifa)
- 2021: Bola de Ouro (France Football) e 2º no The Best (Fifa)
- 2022: Não indicado na Bola de Ouro (France Football) e Melhor do mundo no The Best (Fifa)*

\**Na edição de 2022, a Fifa considerou o período entre agosto de 2021 e dezembro de 2022, e não a temporada 2021/22, como a Bola de Ouro*

# FIFA World Player of the Year Winners

## Quick Answer

Vinícius Júnior, forward for Real Madrid and the Brazil national team, won the 2024 edition of The Best FIFA Men’s Player award.

* Most wins: Lionel Messi leads with 3 Best FIFA Men's Player awards.
* Christiano Ronaldo and Robert Lewandowski follows with 2 Best FIFA Men's Player awards.

## Table of Contents

* [1. Award Overview](#award-overview)
* [2. Complete List of Winners](#complete-winners)
* [3. Statistical Analysis](#statistical-analysis)
* [4. Notable Achievements](#notable-achievements)

* [6. Frequently Asked Questions](#faq-section)

## Award Overview

The [FIFA World Player](/sport/soccer/list-player-of-the-year-fifa.htm) of the Year is one of the most prominent awards in international football. It recognizes the unique genius of players who have excelled throughout the year. The award was first granted in 1991, and soon rose to prominence as a standard for greatness in world football. Players like Lionel Messi, Zinedine Zidane, Ronaldo Nazário, and [Cristiano Ronaldo](/sport/soccer/profiles/ronaldo-cristiano.htm) have cemented their position in football history by winning the trophy numerous times.

It's worth noting that before being restored as a component of The Best FIFA Football Awards, the prize underwent significant changes over time, including its merging with the Ballon d'Or from 2010 to 2015.

> **“Winners are decided by four equally weighted voting groups: national team coaches, captains, selected media representatives, and fans—ensuring a truly global perspective when honoring the best in football.”**

> — *FIFA*, explaining the voting process for *The Best FIFA Football Awards, 2016*

Since 2004, FIFA has used a shortlist system for its top player awards, with nominees selected by FIFA experts before votes are cast by national team captains, coaches, and journalists. This structure was designed to balance input from players, managers, and the media, ensuring broader representation in the decision-making process.

![Cristiano Ronaldo Statue](/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto,width=700,height=394,quality=60,fit=scale-down/global/images/sport_soccer_images_cr7.jpg)

Statue of Cristiano Ronaldo in the harbour of his hometown, Funchal, Madeira

The award underwent a significant transformation from 2010 to 2015 when it merged with the Ballon d'Or to create the [FIFA Ballon d'Or](/sport/soccer/awards/ballondor.htm), before separating again in 2016.

### Award Distribution by Era

The award has been dominated by different players across distinct eras:

* 1991-1999: Nine different winners, with only Ronaldo winning multiple times (1996, 1997)
* 2000-2009: Era of diversity with Zidane, Ronaldinho, and the emergence of Messi
* 2010-2019: The Messi-Ronaldo dominance, winning 9 out of 10 awards
* 2020-2024: New generation emerging with Lewandowski, though Messi continues to win

## Notable Achievements and Records

### Youngest Winner

Ronaldo was just 20 years old when he won his first FIFA World Player of the Year award in 1996, making him the youngest recipient in the award's history.

### Only African Winner

George Weah remains the only African player to win the award, achieving this historic feat in 1995 while representing Liberia.

### Defender Recognition

Fabio Cannavaro's 2006 victory stands out as the only time a defender has won the award, following Italy's World Cup triumph.

### The 2023 Tiebreaker

The 2023 award ceremony featured a historic moment when Lionel Messi and Erling Haaland both received exactly 48 points in the initial voting. According to FIFA regulations, a tiebreaker was required, with the winner determined by which player received more points from national team captains. Messi ultimately prevailed to claim his eighth award.

## Evolution of the Award

### The FIFA Ballon d'Or Era (2010-2015)

From 2010 to 2015, FIFA and France Football magazine merged their respective awards to create the FIFA Ballon d'Or. This collaboration combined the voting mechanisms of both awards, bringing together national team captains, coaches, and international journalists in a unified voting process. During these six years, the award alternated between just two players: Lionel Messi (2010, 2011, 2012, 2015) and Cristiano Ronaldo (2013, 2014).

### The Separation and Modern Era (2016-Present)

In 2016, FIFA and France Football ended their partnership, with each organization returning to their separate awards. FIFA rebranded their award as "The Best FIFA Men's Player," while the Ballon d'Or returned to its traditional format. Despite the separation, both awards have often recognized the same player, with Cristiano Ronaldo winning both in 2016 and 2017, and the awards diverging for the first time in 2018 when Luka Modrić won the FIFA award while the Ballon d'Or went to Modrić as well.

⚠️ Important Note: The 2024 awards saw a divergence between FIFA and the Ballon d'Or, with Vinícius Junior winning the FIFA award while Rodri claimed the Ballon d'Or, distinguishing the different voting criteria and constituencies of each award.

### Voting Process Evolution

The voting process has undergone significant refinements since 2004:

* 1991-2003: National team coaches and captains voted for the winner from an open field of candidates
* 2004-2009: Introduction of a 35-player shortlist, with votes from national team captains, coaches, and journalists.
* 2010-2015: During the FIFA Ballon d'Or era, media representatives were added to the voting panel
* 2016-Present: The current format includes equal weighting between four voting groups: national team captains, national team coaches, media representatives, and online fan voting

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Who has won the most FIFA World Player of the Year awards?

Lionel Messi has won the most awards with 8 total wins (including the FIFA Ballon d'Or years from 2010-2015).

### What's the difference between the FIFA World Player of the Year and the Ballon d'Or?

The FIFA World Player of the Year is voted on by national team captains, coaches, journalists, and fans, while the Ballon d'Or is voted exclusively by journalists. The two awards merged from 2010-2015 as the FIFA Ballon d'Or but have been separate since 2016.

### Has any goalkeeper ever won the FIFA World Player of the Year?

No goalkeeper has ever won the FIFA World Player of the Year award. The closest was Manuel Neuer, who finished third in 2014. Fabio Cannavaro in 2006 remains the only defensive player to win the award.

### Which countries have produced the most FIFA World Player of the Year winners?

Brazil and Argentina each have 8 wins total, though Argentina's are all from Lionel Messi. Brazil has had six different winners: Romário, Ronaldo, Rivaldo, Ronaldinho, Kaká, and Vinícius Junior. Portugal is third with 6 wins (5 from Cristiano Ronaldo, 1 from Luís Figo).

### Who won the 2024 FIFA World Player of the Year?

Vinícius Junior from Brazil won the 2024 FIFA World Player of the Year award. Interestingly, the 2024 Ballon d'Or was won by Rodri from Spain, marking a divergence between the two major individual awards.

### Can players from any league win the FIFA World Player of the Year?

Yes, players from any professional league worldwide are eligible for the FIFA World Player of the Year award. Unlike the original Ballon d'Or (1956-2007), which was restricted to European-based players, the FIFA award has always been open to all professional footballers globally.
